title: LLAMA LIMA: A Living Meta-Analysis on the Effects of Generative AI on Learning Mathematics
extended_summary:
This paper presents LLAMA LIMA, a living meta-analysis focused on the effects of generative AI interventions on mathematics learning. The authors argue that conventional reviews become outdated too quickly in a fast-moving field like generative AI, so they use a continuously updated evidence-synthesis model following PRISMA-LSR guidance. The central question is whether generative AI-based instructional interventions improve mathematics learning outcomes, and eventually which learner, contextual, and design factors moderate those effects.

The approach is a Bayesian multilevel meta-analysis of experimental and quasi-experimental studies comparing generative AI interventions with control conditions that did not use generative AI. For Version 2, the review included 21 studies and 38 effect sizes, based on literature searches through February 2, 2026. The included interventions covered multiple purposes for generative AI in mathematics education, such as mathematics expert tools, adaptive assessment and tutoring, instructional support, collaborative facilitation, and teacher support. The review also included preprints undergoing peer review in order to reduce publication lag.

The evidence base spans a wide range of educational contexts and learner groups, including primary, lower secondary, upper secondary, undergraduate, and adult learners. The included studies came from multiple countries and settings, but this paper synthesizes them at the meta-analytic level rather than reporting one single participant site. The paper also notes that some interventions indirectly involved teachers, especially when generative AI was used for teacher support.

The main finding is a positive pooled effect of generative AI interventions on mathematics learning (Hedges' g = 0.42), with a wide 95% credible interval [0.13, 0.72], indicating meaningful uncertainty and heterogeneity across studies. Publication-bias analyses did not show evidence of strong publication bias. The authors conclude that generative AI may support mathematics learning, but the evidence base is still limited and too heterogeneous to support strong generalizations. They emphasize the need for further rigorous studies and future moderator analyses in later versions of the living meta-analysis.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI systems, including LLM-based tools and chatbots, used in mathematics education for purposes such as tutoring, instruction, feedback, assessment, problem solving support, and related learning assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: This living meta-analysis synthesizes experimental and quasi-experimental studies of generative AI–based interventions for learning mathematics across heterogeneous tools and implementations; it does not report per-tool effect estimates.

findings.finding_summary: Across 21 studies contributing 38 effect sizes and 4,071 participants, generative AI–based instructional interventions showed a positive pooled effect on mathematics learning outcomes (g = 0.42). The 95% credible interval was wide [0.13, 0.72], and the authors note substantial heterogeneity and uncertainty, so conclusions remain tentative.

A publication-bias sensitivity analysis using RoBMA produced a somewhat smaller model-averaged estimate of the effect of generative AI interventions on mathematics learning, g = 0.29, with interval [0.00, 0.68]. The inclusion Bayes factor for publication bias was BF = 0.65 with posterior probability = .39, which the authors interpret as weak evidence against publication bias.
findings.measure: Mathematics learning outcomes / mathematics performance (publication-bias-adjusted model-averaged estimate)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a meta-analysis using PRISMA-LSR procedures and Bayesian multilevel meta-regression across 21 studies, which meets the highest evidence design tier. However, the paper is a living preprint and the evidence base is still limited and heterogeneous.
impact_tier_rationale: The main pooled effect is positive and above the 0.20 threshold (g = 0.42), indicating at least medium impact by the framework's rule. The wide credible interval adds uncertainty, but the reported average effect remains in the blue range.
